title: AI's true target isn't new jobs—it's the clean work outsourced to India a decade ago
dek: Work with clear boundaries, verifiable results, and single tasks was already shipped to India; now AI takes over. What actually resists AI is messy work that runs on relationships and political deal-making.
why: The first 35 minutes dissect Spanish housing, pensions, party discipline, and the EU's veto power—dense, regional economics. The last 15 minutes are an economist's counterintuitive case on AI and employment; they carry the episode's highest yield.
who: Anyone tracking European political economy and labor-market reform, and anyone who wants to understand AI's real impact on employment without the ‘mass unemployment’ narrative.
skip: 30:24–35:00 overrated/underrated segment and Spanish language-change discussion signal little; skip them.

points.h: Spain's building capacity collapsed after the crisis
points.body: Before 2008, Spain completed up to 800,000 housing units yearly, with elastic land supply. After the bubble burst, the public linked easy construction approval to corruption and rising prices; the central government clamped down on local land approvals. Now, with tens of thousands of immigrants arriving yearly, Spain builds under 100,000 units a year. Notably, there is no YIMBY movement in Spain—not even Garicano himself publicly advocates for more building.

points.h: Spain is governed by and for the elderly
points.body: Spain has the world's 5th-lowest fertility rate and 5th-highest life expectancy. Since 2008, essentially all GDP growth has flowed to pensions, not productive investment. High-speed rail and motorways are well-developed; the investments the country actually needs are scarce. Garicano's conclusion is direct: Spain is currently ruled by and for its retired, elderly population.

points.h: The Basque Country's fiscal privilege rests on invented history
points.body: The Basque region was granted autonomous tax collection and separate negotiation with the central government—a federal-style fiscal arrangement—because of past terrorism. By timing negotiations just before votes that could topple the government, the Basque Country has frozen its remittance to Madrid. As pensions rise nationwide, the Basque Country pays nothing extra; it has become a net beneficiary. Catalonia demands the same deal, but its size means the same arrangement would break the national budget. Unsolvable.

points.h: Parties promote the trapped, not the talented
points.body: Garicano's time in politics revealed that the real mechanism linking voters to parties is internal discipline. Parties advance not the smartest policy designers, but people who have nowhere else to go—those who will never rebel because leaving the party means losing everything. The same logic explains how the EU Commission picks its president: member states choose candidates who don't threaten them, not the most capable person.

points.h: The EU veto locked defense and tax to unanimity
points.body: The EU uses majority voting on the single market but retains unanimity on core sovereignty: tax, defense, foreign policy. Each country wants final say, so they buy tanks, jets, and ammunition separately—artillery shells come in incompatible calibers. Weeks of negotiation just to settle 55mm versus 55.5mm. Garicano is clear: if he could press a button to swap unanimity for a two-thirds supermajority, he would press it.

points.h: Rigid labor law's real cost is the price of error
points.body: Europe's strict firing protections don't just raise hiring costs—companies can cut salaries to offset that. The actual killer is making mistakes expensive. Facebook realized the metaverse was wrong and disbanded the team in a week, then hired an AI team. Ericsson or Nokia would spend months in union talks before laying anyone off; by then, the company might be dead. The company can't afford the pivot.

points.h: AI will first devour the work outsourced to India a decade ago
points.body: Garicano and his coauthor's core claim: AI will empty not messy work, but the kind of work that was mass-outsourced to India—clean boundaries, single tasks, verifiable output. This work was always easy for companies to define precisely and ship out; now AI takes over. Reinforcement learning trains directly on verifiable outcomes. Messy work that requires managing relationships and political maneuvering? That stays.

points.h: Productivity gains evaporated into the hallway
points.body: A Chinese IT executive told Garicano that every employee's individual efficiency is rising, but the whole IT department's output hasn't budged. The productivity gains, she said, are being extracted ‘in the hallway’. A study of doctors using AI transcription tools showed doctors see more patients, but some use the freed time for yoga class—leisure gains exist, but get converted into ‘do a bit more’ rather than ‘rest a bit more’.
